articles.summary: Michelle Metcalf didn’t initially plan to work in forestry. Growing up on a farm in Walnut Grove, Minnesota, far from any forests, she headed to college as a pharmacy major. But after connecting with people in the forestry program at the University of Montana, everything changed.
articles.title: Michelle Metcalf Brings Sustainability to Life Across Western Timberlands

articles.summary: As winter loosens its grip across our Canadian timberlands, another season quickly comes into focus — wildfire season — and spring offers a critical window to transition and prepare for drier conditions. Across regions, our teams update plans, test equipment, refresh training and reconnect with partners. The goal is simple: be ready to act before the first spark.
articles.title: Image of a helicopter in the distance as it prepares to land, with individuals wearing protective gear (vests and hard hats) await its arrival.

articles.summary: Dumping hoppers are a fixture at our Panels facilities — they’re affixed to forklifts and used daily to move ash, sawdust and other materials around the site. But each time an operator dumped the hopper’s load, they had to climb out of the forklift and manually work the latch — exposing them to multiple potential hazards, that could result in slips, trips and falls or even finger amputation.
articles.title: A Smarter, Safer Way to Dump a Hopper — Without Ever Leaving Your Seat
